title: The lane-archive guard reads a public repo's open PRs anonymously, and its refusal names the add_repo access push route for a private repo
why: lane-closes-after-records refused three times tonight on lane session-mailbox-followups because this session could not read the lane's second repo; add_repo fixed it at 09:08 CST. The owner asked (09:12 CST) that the fix be mechanical.
source: retrospective 09:13 CST Nov 13, owner ask 09:12 CST
note: Fix: when the archive guard cannot read a lane repo, its refusal names the act 'add_repo <owner>/<repo> access push, then retry', with the repo from the lane's cs-repo tag. Red first: a fixture lane whose repo read fails gets that remedy. The gap itself (archive-guard-child-repo-read) is a debt for the lane to file on main. 13:14 CST Nov 17 (coordinator relay, filed by triage 11): hook lane-closes-after-records refused archive_session twice, "the open pull requests of the lane's repo (shivinate7/mailaudit) could not be read". Measured by the coordinator: add_repo access read attaches nothing for a public repo, so the guard's gh could not read its PRs; access push fixed it. So the planned remedy text must say access push, not (read), and the guard could read a public repo's open PRs anonymously over REST. The owner asked how to resolve this mechanically (13:10 CST); page item 937 asks which of three fixes. Ruling: owner 13:11 CST Nov 17, typed in the coordinator's chat and relayed (page item 937 closed on option a, "approved"; not read by triage as typed): the guard reads a public repo's open PRs anonymously over REST; the refusal for a private repo says "attach with add_repo access push, then retry". The planned text "(read)" is now "access push". A guard change: test-author red case first (a public repo reads with no attach; a private repo that cannot read gets the remedy), review rounds apply.
